articles.title: NC State and Philip Rivers reportedly negotiating deal to make him the Wolfpack's next head coach
articles.summary: Rivers played at NC State from 2000-2003 and his son is committed to join the team in 2027.
articles.body:
NC State isn't wasting much time working to make Philip Rivers its next head coach.

According to On3 , the longtime NFL quarterback and NC State alum is "working to finalize a deal" to be the Wolfpack's head coach after the 2026 season. Rivers is currently coaching high school football at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama.

Rivers immediately emerged as a candidate for the job after the firing of Dave Doeren. NC State moved on from Doeren after more than 13 years following a 3-4 start to the season that included a nearly unfathomable loss to Vanderbilt.

Before the porous start to 2026, Doeren's teams had won at least eight games in five of the last six seasons. NC State was blown out by Duke on Saturday to fall to 4-5.

Rivers' potential hire would be a boost for the Wolfpack in an ACC that looks more wide-open than ever behind Miami. As the Hurricanes have emerged as the top program in the conference, Clemson is struggling to reach the heights it did before the NIL era and Florida State is also in the midst of an athletic department transition as it looks for a new athletic director and a coach to succeed Mike Norvell.

Rivers played four seasons at NC State from 2000 through 2003 before he was the No. 4 overall pick of the 2004 NFL Draft. He was initially selected by the Giants and traded to the Chargers as part of the draft day deal that sent Eli Manning to New York because of his refusal to play for the Chargers.

As a senior, Rivers was the 2003 ACC player of the year and finished seventh in the Heisman voting. He threw for nearly 4,500 yards and 34 TDs while completing over 70% of his passes.

He's also just a year removed from last playing in the NFL. Rivers briefly ended his four-year NFL retirement at the end of the 2025 season to play three games for the Indianapolis Colts as they looked for a stopgap solution at quarterback following Daniel Jones' Achilles injury. Rivers had last played for the Colts in 2020 after 16 seasons with the Chargers.

Making Rivers the team's head coach would also save NC State from a potential high-profile de-commitment from its 2027 recruiting class. Rivers' son Gunner is the No. 12 QB in the class of 2027 and verbally committed to NC State in February. Gunner Rivers plays at St. Michael for his father.

In addition to considering Rivers for the job, NC State also reportedly talked to former Wolfpack quarterback Russell Wilson about the job. Unlike Rivers, who has no college coaching experience but has been a high school head coach since 2021, Wilson doesn't have any coaching experience, having moved into TV for CBS after concluding his playing career at the end of the 2025 season.

Wilson's CBS coworker Bill Cowher also played a key role in the coaching search. After Doeren's firing, NC State AD Boo Corrigan said that the former Steelers coach and former NFL defensive back Dewayne Washington would assist him in finding the team's next head coach.

articles.title: Hearts 2-5 Falkirk: Bairns end Jambos impressive home Premiership record to replace them in third
articles.summary: Report as Falkirk beat Hearts 5-2 at Tynecastle Park; Finley Barbrook opened the scoring with Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell's double putting them five in front; Sabri Guendouz and Claudio Braga pulled two goals back for the Jambos
articles.body:
Wouter Vrancken's beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell's double.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday's Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns are now one point above Hearts after their fifth straight Premiership victory.

"This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure. Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

"When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It's childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

"It's crazy, crazy, and everybody - me, staff, players - have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous."

On losing defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott to injury, Vrancken added: "This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again.

"Hopefully it's not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who were good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level."

"I've never been 5-0 up here before. First half, we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

"It was well documented about the Hearts injuries and, coming off the back of the game on Thursday night (in Thun), it was always going to be difficult for them.

"We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that's exactly what happened. The goals and our play were outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

"We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. At 3pm, we never expected to be 4-0 up at half-time and certainly not 5-0 up a few minutes into the second half, which was another really good goal in transition.

"Hearts had a lot at the ball and dominated the second period, but we're taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it. It jumps us up into third place.

"Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies' team, so I'm delighted for everyone at the football club that we've managed to equal that record."

articles.title: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson back to his best while Chelsea go back to square one - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers analyse Sunday's Premier League action as Alisson stars in Liverpool's win at Crystal Palace, Chelsea are out-muscled at Sunderland, Brentford's ill-discipline costs them against Brighton, and Bournemouth are on a roll...
articles.body:
Liverpool hit three at Palace, with three £100m+ players - Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and, with an assist, Bradley Barcola - involved in the goals. But it was their goalkeeper Alisson who was Liverpool's best performer.

Crystal Palace will be so frustrated because on another day, the narrative could have swung their way. But the brilliant Brazilian delivered in key moments in the game.

His save from Daichi Kamada's volley was an exceptional reaction stop. Two minutes later Liverpool took the lead.

Alisson was then at full stretch to push away Adam Wharton's header to ensure Liverpool went into the break with the advantage. And on 77 minutes, with the score 2-0, he prevented Yeremy Pino from setting up a grandstand finish by shutting down the angle to save the one-on-one.

Alisson may have had fortune with Pino hitting the bar when he was beaten early in the contest and he lost out on a clean sheet due to a controversial late Eddie Nketiah penalty, but in between he reminded everyone why he has been the Premier League's standout goalkeeper since his arrival in 2018. Peter Smith

Just when you think Chelsea are about to change and show some form, they go right back to square one.

They went into the last international break on the back of a damning 3-0 defeat to Brentford, where without star man Joao Pedro, they were bullied, outfought and deservedly beaten by the Bees .

Sunderland, who started the day bottom of the table, are now another team in red and white who have overpowered them to three points - right in time for the next international break.

In the first half, Chelsea lost 63 per cent of the duels as Brian Brobbey wreaked havoc on the Blues backline. This time it was Levi Colwill who was showing defensive frailties as he was hooked off at half-time, with Wesley Fofana the culprit of some unpunished blunders against Manchester United last week.

Ultimately, this match showed that Chelsea don't have enough defensive solidity and the injured Pedro is their most important player. But we've known that for weeks. More concerningly, Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea team were "not bullied" despite the eye test and the data backing it up.

The first part of solving these problems is recognising they exist. Until that changes, Chelsea will always end up going the same places.

They are now outside the top four, and with Everton and Bournemouth picking up form behind them, they are drifting towards the middle of the table again. Sam Blitz

While Sunderland's defensive solidity to beat Chelsea owed everything to a team effort, there was no-one taking the credit for their best attacking performance of the season away from Brian Brobbey.

Even ignoring the big Dutchman's role in winning the penalty for Sunderland's winner, it was testament to his unrivalled threat that Xabi Alonso sacrificed Moises Caicedo from his midfield to shackle the forward at half-time.

Brobbey is unparalleled in what he does across the Premier League. He has held the ball up 31 times this season, comfortably more than anyone else despite missing two of 10 matchdays with injury.

He is the only player to have completed 10 or more hold-ups where more than half have retained possession - and he keeps it almost 70 per cent of the time.

Sunderland fans were delighted to see the 24-year-old sign a new deal on Wearside earlier this week despite only scoring in one game this season. But his game is about so much more.

Roy Keane described his bustling run to win Sunday's penalty as "brilliant centre-forward play". Chris Sutton said he "bullied" Fofana. That feels a fitting description.

Sunderland's first concern for their survival hopes must be to keep up their rediscovered defensive compactness to stop leaking goals at an unsustainable rate.

But at the other end, so long as Brobbey is fit and firing they will be a nuisance for anyone. Ron Walker

Crystal Palace delivered arguably their best performance of the season against Liverpool but still lost 3-1. Pierre Sage has not lost the players but may well lose his job.

Bottom of the table after 10 games and, alarmingly, Palace have conceded more goals at this stage of a league season than they have for 25 years.

Sage's porous defence have shipped 24 goals in the Premier League. That is what will cost him his job if, indeed, he is to be sacked.

Palace came close to scoring on three occasions in the first half against Liverpool only to be undone by the simplest of free-kick routines. That is the sixth non-penalty set piece Palace have conceded this season.

It is a pattern that they cannot afford to keep repeating. Zinny Boswell

Across their first five Premier League seasons combined - 190 games - Brentford players were shown a total of eight red cards. With 10 games gone in 2026/27, they have already been shown three - and they have all come in their last three games.

Vitaly Janelt's late dismissal at home to Liverpool on October 17 was the result of a second booking. There's nothing really to discuss in that case.

But earlier in that game, Yehor Yarmoliuk was shown a straight red, after a VAR review, for headbutting Jeremy Jacquet . "I do think they were cute, clever - but Yarmo needs to do better," said Bees boss Keith Andrews afterwards.

Brentford were leading at that point and looking good value for their advantage, but the red changed the game and they conspired to lose 2-1.

Against Brighton, they were 1-0 down when Igor Thiago was shown a straight red after catching Chema in the face with his arm, splitting his opponent's lip in the process. Again, referee Michael Oliver was sent to the monitor, where he upgraded his original decision - and again, there was no way back for Brentford.

For a team that has a tendency to drop points from winning positions, this recent lack of discipline is another thing hindering their positive start. Dan Long

European football is supposed to come with a health warning. More games, more travel, more tired legs and, supposedly, a dip in domestic performance. Somebody should tell Bournemouth.

They have played nine times in the last month and have won eight of their last eight. That is an extraordinary return given the relentless schedule.

There is clearly something working brilliantly behind the scenes at the club. Whether it is the conditioning, recovery methods, squad management or simply the infectious culture the players have, Bournemouth look anything but a team running on empty.

Ipswich were the latest to discover that. The 2-1 scoreline was flattering to Gary O'Neil's side, who were second best for large spells and struggled to live with Bournemouth's intensity. The gulf in energy levels was striking.

Bournemouth are not just surviving the extra workload, they are thriving on it. Lewis Jones

Ipswich have a Enciso problem. More specifically, they have a problem when Enciso is thwarted.

The Paraguayan has become the creative heartbeat of the newly-promoted team but Bournemouth exposed the danger of building so much of an attacking gameplan around one player. Shut off the supply line to Enciso and suddenly Ipswich look rather ordinary. There was precious little invention elsewhere.

Despite trailing for almost the entire contest, Ipswich mustered just 0.30 expected goals from open play. Even more damning, they failed to register a single touch inside the Bournemouth penalty area in the second half until Clarke converted his penalty in the 73rd minute.

That is quite some attacking impotence when you are chasing a game.

Ipswich cannot afford to be so predictable.

Premier League opponents will have watched that performance closely. The blueprint is out there. Ipswich need a plan B. Lewis Jones

On the face of it, a win over Roma and a draw with Aston Villa might represent two encouraging results to calm some of the noise around Manchester United. Fat chance. So messy have these Old Trafford games been there are more questions than answers.

At least Michael Carrick's players have put to bed the idea that they do not want to put the work in. Two dramatic comebacks are a testament to their resilience and their willingness to dig themselves out of the biggest holes even as the atmosphere turns.

In that sense, they seem with their coach. But the fact that they have found themselves two goals behind on three separate occasions in two games suggests that major issues remain. United are so chaotic in their setup. It is why they are in the relegation zone.

It says a lot that even in a week in which they have somewhat arrested the decline following the home defeat to Bournemouth, United have still conceded more goals than they have scored in those three games - and they have scored seven. Too many errors.

Supporters are sick of Diogo Dalot making them. But can there be any surprise that Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven make for an uncertain centre-back pairing at this level? Neither man has yet celebrated his 21st birthday. Squad building Manchester United style.

There is enough quality at United, enough support to ensure that the magical moments keep coming. But the strange mood upon the final whistle betrayed the reality. Ten games into the season they are one point off the bottom of the Premier League table.

There was a number of elements to Aston Villa's late collapse that allowed Manchester United to come back from two down for the second time in one afternoon. But ultimately Zion Suzuki's unconvincing goalkeeping proved costly for Unai Emery's side.

The Japanese goalkeeper had made a promising start to life at Villa Park after replacing the experienced figure of Emiliano Martinez. Suzuki looks particularly strong with his feet. But after an error against Fulham, this display showed that there is much learn.

There were bumps from Matheus Cunha and goalkeeping counterpart Senne Lammens Emery pointed out that these might have been enough to earn a free-kick in other leagues. But they were not really enough to stop Suzuki from dealing with the ball.

Suzuki, 24, will need to adapt. Emery is convinced that he will. "Zion is going to improve, adapting to the Premier League, but during the process we conceded one more. But Zion is very fantastic how he is performing." Even so, he cost Villa the win at Old Trafford.

articles.summary: El Castilla tuvo que neutralizar en dos ocasiones la ventaja obtenida por el Hércules en cada una de las partes
articles.body: Empate del Castilla en la visita que rindió el Hércules al Di Stéfano, donde marcó dos goles en sus dos únicas ocasiones. Máxima efectividad visitante que tuvo que ser neutralizada por los blancos a base de trabajo e insistencia para sumar un punto de mérito en su feudo. Los tantos de Aguado y Cestero por parte madridista igualaron los de Antoñín y Soldevila. Empezó el Castilla frío, encajando casi en la primera llegada herculana. Un centro lateral de Víctor Narro llegó hasta Antoñín, que se había situado perfectamente tras Fortea para lograr rematar a gol. Aún estaban los de López de Lerma tomando posiciones y ya llegaba el primer jarro de agua fría. De nuevo la meta blanca perforada y otra vez tocaba remontar para optar a sumar algún punto. Pero las escasas llegadas del filial lo ponían todo un poco más cuesta arriba. El Hércules tenía controlado un encuentro en el que apenas se estaba viendo exigido. Cuando la segunda mitad parecía que iba por los mismos derroteros, llegó el empuje y la jugada personal de Diego Aguado, que inicia una potente conducción en el costado zurdo para en carrera ir cayendo al interior, adentrándose en área, y sorprender al meta Abad por el hueco que dejó junto al palo. Un empate que dio energía al filial, que empezó a gozar de distintas ocasiones en los siguientes minutos. El Hércules ahora sí sufría y veía peligrar la victoria. Carvajal estuvo a punto de conseguir el segundo tanto castillista de cabeza en el 72’, aunque el equipo alicantino estuvo muy certero en las acciones defensivas y sobre todo efectivo, ya que en una de las escasas acciones a balón parado a su favor cerca del área de Mestre, consiguió Soldevila en un magistral libre directo el gol que parecía de la victoria a pocos minutos para el final. Sin embargo la garra del filial provocó el tanto de Cestero en el 90’, al rematar en el área la asistencia de Leiva. articles.title: Celtic 1-0 Kilmarnock: Liam Scales restores Hoops' four-point Premiership lead with winner against struggling Killie
articles.summary: Report as Celtic beat Kilmarnock 1-0 to restore their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership; Liam Scales scored after Kasper Hogh's opener was disallowed; Benjamin Nygren missed a penalty; Kilmarnock are bottom of the table
articles.body:
Liam Scales hooked Camilo Duran cross into the top corner in the 26th minute as they head into the international break after back-to-back wins.

Celtic - and Kasper Hogh in particular - otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

After a silence for Remembrance Sunday was cut short after boos from the stands, Kilmarnock came close.

Tom Lowery forced Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone into a double save before Hogh saw an early goal ruled out as his goalless run extended to 16 games, having last found the net with a hat-trick against Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

The Danish striker finished from seven yards after being set up by Nygren and ran to the standing section to celebrate.

His joy was short-lived as referee John Beaton was summoned to the monitor and gave a free-kick to Killie for Mika Baur's challenge on Greg Kiltie.

Killie had some good first-half chances and Celtic could not get the two-goal cushion in a dominant second half.

The champions were nearly made to pay in stoppage time, but Ieuan Owen could not make any contact with Erik Ring's inviting cross inside the six-yard box.

The Rugby Park side are bottom of the table heading into the break, winless in their last four games.

1: SAVE! Sam Johnstone is called into action early. He gets down to save Tom Lowery's first effort, then reacts quickly to deny him again.

13: GOAL CELTIC! Kasper Hogh breaks the deadlock, but referee John Beaton is called to the monitor.

15: NO GOAL! Hugh's strike is ruled out for Mika Baur's foul on Greg Kiltie in the build-up.

26: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran sends the ball into the box, Liam Scales sticks out his leg and the ball loops into the net.

28: SAVE! Michael Schjonning-Larsen has a go from distance, but Johnstone pushes it clear.

51: CLOSE! Colby Donovan is just inches from doubling Celtic's lead.

53: SAVE! Duran's curling effort from outside the box is saved by Nico Mantl.

57: OVER! Hogh's powerful strike from just inside the box flies over the bar.

75: PENALTY TO CELTIC! Replays show the ball hit Aaron Tshibola's arm and the referee points to the spot.

76: PENALTY MISSED! Benjamin Nygren steps up but his shot is saved by Mantl.

90+1: CLOSE! Erik Ring sends in a low ball and Ieuan Owen is inches away from knocking it in.

O'Neill delighted to see international break

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was a tough game for us. Very, very tough.

"Sam Johnstone pulled us out in the first minute of the game with a great double save.

"Like everything else, I think any manager would say about his team, of course. There's things that we can definitely do much, much better. But overall, delighted.

"Delighted with the effort that they put in because we've been going now. We've been going mid-week, weekend, mid-week, weekend.

"It's been tough, tough on us really, but that's what you try to do.

"You're in the game to try and compete in European football if you can and then obviously keep an eye on domestic things at the same time.

"I'm delighted that we are in the position that we're in."

'So many good things' for McCann, despite defeat

Kilmarnock manager Neil McCann speaking to Sky Sports News:

"I thought the boys deserved to take something from the game.

"Disappointed with the nature of the goal, again, that we can see, but so many good things to take from today. The chances at either side of the match, early in the match we probably had two or three and then right at the death there.

"There's been a wee bit of a narrative going around that this team's under pressure and I know they are playing under pressure a wee bit, because we're not getting results that I believe that our performances have deserved. But they come here and they played with bravery to get the ball down, play the way we want to play, still have a threat over the top that we need to have.

"It tells me how much they're developing as a team, that they're in the dressing room disappointed, looking like they've taken nothing from the game, because I think they did deserve it.

"I don't want to be sitting here and be a glorious loser.

"We want to come and get something from the game. I feel that the boys probably deserved it and a balance of play, but so much to like and so much to look forward to after our national break."

articles.title: Infantino’s Japanese challenger claims he could unseat FIFA president
articles.summary: Kozo Tashima believes he has a ’20 to 30 percent’ chance of winning the FIFA presidency election against Infantino.
articles.body:
The latest challenger to FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s re-election bid, Kozo Tashima, believes he has a 20 to 30 percent chance of winning the coveted seat in global football.

Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), said governance is FIFA’s biggest problem as he outlined his platform for next year’s presidential election on Sunday.

“I’ve received many messages saying, ‘Thank you for speaking out’…,” Tashima told Japanese daily Sports Nippon.

Tashima announced on Thursday that he intended to run in the March election , becoming the first Japanese candidate to seek world football’s top job.

The 68-year-old former Japan international has served on the FIFA Council since 2015 and became JFA president the following year before being succeeded by Tsuneyasu Miyamoto in 2024.

“I’ve been contacted by presidents and international department officials from eight countries, including some outside Asia,” he said.

“While I haven’t received any formal endorsements yet, I’m getting a positive response. Since time is short and I don’t want to be held up by incomplete paperwork, I want to secure support from at least six associations.”

Tashima requires nominations from five national associations, a prerequisite for standing in the election.

Candidates have until November 18 to submit nominations for the election, in which Infantino is seeking a fourth term as head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino came under scrutiny in July after an unsuccessful attempt to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions including the World Cup.

Despite the criticism, Infantino’s candidacy received a significant boost in October when the head of Asian football publicly endorsed him , while support from several FIFA confederations has left him well placed among the organisation’s 211 member associations.

“I’ll keep what’s good and change what’s bad…,” Tashima added. “The biggest problem, however, remains governance…

“Selflessness is my motto… At this stage, I think my chances of winning are about 20 to 30 percent, but as the campaign progresses, I want to raise my confidence to 40 or 50 percent. I truly want to change FIFA.”

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his intention to challenge fellow Swiss citizen Infantino last month.

articles.title: Sergio Lobera regresa a Ceuta ante el reto de lograr la permanencia
articles.standfirst: El entrenador aragonés ya entrenó al equipo caballa en la temporada 2011-2012
articles.summary: El entrenador aragonés ya entrenó al equipo caballa en la temporada 2011-2012
articles.body: Tras consumarse la salida de José Juan Romero, el Ceuta ha movido ficha con rapidez en el mercado de banquillos. La entidad caballa ha hecho oficial el fichaje de Sergio Lobera como nuevo entrenador del primer equipo hasta el final de la presente temporada, firmando un contrato que incluye la opción de prorrogarse por un año más. El técnico maño asume la dirección del bando blanco con la urgencia de enderezar el rumbo de un equipo hundido en el farolillo rojo con sólo 5 puntos. Para Lobera supone el retorno a un entorno bien conocido, ya que dirigió al conjunto ceutí en la campaña 2011-2012. Tras aquel periplo, dio el salto a la Segunda división española para llevar las riendas de la UD Las Palmas durante dos ejercicios consecutivos en los que metió al cuadro canario en los playoffs de ascenso. A partir de ahí, el preparador aragonés inició un extenso recorrido internacional que le llevó al Moghreb Atlético de Tetuán —alcanzando los cuartos de final de la Champions africana—, así como al FC Goa en India, donde se proclamó campeón de la Supercopa. Su trayectoria continuó bajo el paraguas del City Football Group dirigiendo al Mumbai City FC (con el que conquistó el título de Liga) y posteriormente al Sichuan Jiuniu chino, antes de asumir su último reto en el Odisha FC de la Superliga india. En su nueva etapa en el Alfonso Murube, Sergio Lobera estará acompañado por una representación de la casa. David Polaco, con quien coincidió en su etapa de formación en La Masía, ejercerá como segundo entrenador. La parcela técnica se completará con la continuidad de Reda al frente de la preparación de porteros, Luis Enrique Ramos como preparador físico y la dupla formada por Ezequiel Gómez y Raúl Alcázar en el análisis táctico. Desde el seno del club se destaca el firme compromiso mostrado por el técnico aragonés desde el primer momento. Tras iniciarse las conversaciones en la noche de ayer y extenderse las reuniones hasta la madrugada y la mañana de hoy, Lobera trasladó su predisposición y un conocimiento amplio de la plantilla, la institución y la ciudad para capitanear la reacción del equipo.

articles.title: Íñigo le debe un café a Buchanan
articles.standfirst: Un gol del canadiense le da aire al entrenador de un Villarreal que ganó muy apurado a un Getafe que no ofreció demasiado
articles.summary: Un gol del canadiense le da aire al entrenador de un Villarreal que ganó muy apurado a un Getafe que no ofreció demasiado
articles.body: El Villarreal lo vio negro, mucho, pero salvó un punto de partido de manual. Un gol de Buchanan, cuando se habían jugado 80 minutos soporíferos, le dio los tres puntos a los amarillos cuando todas las miradas y los pitos de La Cerámica se habían dirigido ya al banquillo. El gol del canadiense le da una bola extra a Íñigo, al que se le había nublado el futuro. Al técnico le queda mucho para encontrar el rendimiento real de su plantilla, pero al menos se marcha al parón con el cargo asegurado y con tiempo para intentar darle la vuelta al juego. El gol de Romero, tras una acción de fantasía de Ayoze cerró el marcador y la agonía Un espuelazo de Mouriño con estirada de Soria fue lo único rescatable de una primera mitad soporífera. De hecho fue el único disparo a puerta y llegó ya en el añadido. Desembarcaba el Villarreal en el estadio de La Cerámica dañado. Cuatro días antes los amarillos se habían llevado la peor paliza de su historia en Europa y esas cosas dejan secuelas. Además en el ambiente estaba el posible despido de Íñigo Pérez en caso de sumar una nueva derrota. En ese escenario, el Getafe salió a lo suyo: balón para el rival y a esperar errores. El partido salió espeso como el buen chocolate. Nada por unos y nada por otros. Más de 25 minutos sin ver a los porteros hasta que Mikautadze descorchara un recorte imposible dentro del área cuyo centro estuvo a punto de rematar a gol Buchanan si no hubiera sido por el despeje sobre la línea de Mojica. La ocasión más clara se la apuntaban los locales que apostaban todo a una combinación de Moleiro, jugando con total libertad. En los de Bordalás solo las arrancadas por banda derecha del reconvertido Andrés García daban sensación de poder generar peligro. El técnico del Getafe no tiene extremos pero con el ex del Levante, actual jugador del Aston Villa, se ha inventado una solución de urgencia de nivel. Pasada la media hora del partido llegó la jugada polémica del choque. Mario Martín le soltó el brazo a Maciá sin balón. El colegiado le sacó amarilla, pero los jugadores del Villarreal pidieron roja. El colegiado consultó al VAR pero lo dejó en la sanción mínima. Al menos, discutible. Sin cambios en el horizonte una falta de Djene en la frontal sobre Gueye abrió la puerta para que los locales desatascaran la cosa a balón parado. El disparo de Gueye pegó en la cabeza de Mario que desvió a córner. A falta de juego, llegaron algunos enganchones. Un posible penalti sobre Moleiro generó una pequeña tangana en el área que no fue a más. La entrada de Ramón Terrats al campo, para protegerse de una posible segunda amarilla a Mario Martín, le sentó bien al Getafe que dio más sensación de peligro en cinco minutos de la segunda mitad que en toda la primera parte. Los de Bordalás se estiraban con algo más de confianza y a los locales se les iba haciendo bola el choque a toda velocidad. En ese escenario apareció un pie milagroso de David Soria para frustrar la mejor ocasión de Gueye. La oportunidad espoleó algo a los locales que apretaron el acelerador mientras los madrileños se hacían fuertes en su propia área. El Villarreal atacaba de forma más continua, más fluida, pero sus llegadas se quedaban en balas de fogueo, sin peligro real. En ese guión, cuando más cómodo parecía estar el Getafe, llegó el tanto de Buchanan, el que más lo había buscado por parte de los locales. Pese al gol al Getafe no le daba para intentar darle la vuelta a la cosa y en la última acción del partido Romero aprovechó un pase de maestro de Ayoze para celebrar los 1.000 partidos en primera con una victoria.

articles.title: Unai Emery: Aston Villa boss reveals why he went down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time in eight-goal thriller at Man Utd
articles.summary: Unai Emery headed down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time after Man Utd rescued a 4-4 draw against his Aston Villa team; Patrick Dorgu scored late equaliser in thrilling contest; Villa director of football operations Damian Vidagany questioned legitimacy of last goal
articles.body:
Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery.

The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended.

Villa have complained about the legitimacy of United's fourth goal - with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens accused of impeding with Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he competed with Dorgu for the corner.

Asked if Emery walking down the tunnel was due to the emotional about the goal standing "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing."

When asked if he felt the goal being awarded was unfair, Emery replied: "No, no. Not unfair. Please.

"They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off."

Full transcript of Emery's prickly interview

Sky reporter Patrick Davison: Does today happen because you're a new team or young side? It is an experience they have to learn from?

PD: Does history play a part, we spoke before the match that Aston Villa don't have a good record here.

UE: "We are in our way and we might be positive, even with this defeat [draw]. We have to be moving on with the process we have."

PD: Last one Unai, we saw you left before the end while VAR were...

UE: "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I think the match was finishing."

PD: You brought something up that I wasn't expecting. Did you think the goal was unfair?

UE: "They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.

"My English is so poor, but it's clear or not?"

UE: "Ok. Thank you, thank you very much. More questions?"

UE: "No? Thank you very much. Have a good Sunday."

Villa chief complains about equaliser standing

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany took to social media to show his dismay at United's last-gasp equaliser against his team being allowed to stand.

United goalkeeper Lammens - who went up for the corner - made contact with Suzuki whilst not looking at the ball, which left Villa furious. VAR checked and cleared Lammens' involvement in the goal.

Sky Sports' Roy Keane says "football is a contact sport" which means the goal should be allowed to stand.

However, Vidagany posted on X: "To put in context this convenient narrative of 'contact sport' we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

"Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

"Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

"But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact."

Emery admitted his anger at seeing Villa throw away their significant advantages at Old Trafford - but revealed his anger was not directed at his players.

"Angry, of course," he said in his press conference. "To accept to lose in the last minutes two goals, it is difficult.

"I am angry for the situation, not with the players. We lost the opportunity to have two points more."

Asked how United were allowed to come back into the game, Emery replied: "They did the same here against Roma with the supporters pushing, they were playing with heart.

"The last moments when we were close to finishing the match, with [Patrick] Dorgu left side, we couldn't defend him good.

"The last corner we were focusing on the adaptation, protecting them to try to avoid the block. Zion [Suzuki] is going to improve, adapting to the Premier League, but during the process we conceded one more.

"But Zion is very fantastic how he is performing."

November 24: Galatasaray (a), Champions League

November 28: Ipswich (a) - live on Sky Sports

December 2: Everton (h) - live on Sky Sports

articles.title: Michael Carrick: Manchester United boss 'expects' to stay on despite club sitting in relegation zone after Aston Villa draw
articles.summary: Manchester United sit third-bottom in the Premier League after a dramatic 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa; Man Utd boss Michael Carrick  'expects' to stay on despite club sitting in relegation zone amid an eight-game winless league run
articles.body:
Man Utd scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point against Villa, but the draw leaves Carrick's side third-bottom and a point from safety.

Man Utd's 18th-place position is their lowest after 10 top-flight games since 1986/87, when they were 20th.

The draw against Villa extends Man Utd's winless run in the league to eight games - a club record in the Premier League era - raising further doubts over Carrick's position heading into the two-week November international break.

When questioned on his future by Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick engaged in a tetchy back-and-forth, insisting he would remain in charge.

PD: "What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? If you thought walking away was the best thing, you'd probably do it."

PD: " What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?

MC: "You're telling me what you think, aren't you?"

PD: "I'm asking you what you think? What do you expect to happen?"

MC: "We understand the situation; we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward and keep working on things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."

Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.

"One hundred per cent," he said. "I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times…

"I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games."

"Football is about moments, football is about what happens in both boxes in the end," Carrick added.

"Take (away) the moments and the totally avoidable goals we've given away, I actually thought we played pretty well, we were the better team for the most part and I'm disappointed we haven't won the game."

Neville: 'Ownership don't have a clue what to do' on Carrick

"You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years - that's not the answer.

"Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don't know. The ownership don't have a clue what to do.

"It's rinse and repeat. (Ruben) Amorim, (Erik) Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success; there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well.

"None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you've got a poor performance department, a poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail.

"Every organisation in the world will fail if you've not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom - your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

"There are real issues within that football club; you've got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions."

Keane: 'Politician' Carrick 'better get moving' on improvements

"It's obviously difficult for the manager. Under pressure, no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn't say much. I don't know if that's a tactic. Like a politician.

"He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there's things we need to work on, but they better get moving on that.

"It's the worst start in how many years; all these stats aren't very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it's just going to continue.

"What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.

"I admire people who are maybe casual. I wish I was casual like that! I see Carrick, and he's like, 'We just have to tighten up'. I'm going, 'Tighten up? You should be banging heads!'

"We're all different, but put it this way, they're going to Liverpool in a few weeks. How many chances are Liverpool going to get? I don't think this is a top Liverpool team, but do you believe United are going to roll their sleeves up and get a clean sheet? Dig in deep? Be hard to beat? Start quick? Well, good luck with that one.

"I don't see that as an honest dressing room. The really top players put demands on each other. They all seem to be tiptoeing around each other.

"They are certainly lacking leaders in the dressing room."

articles.title: CFP Playoff Bracket, Scenarios and Bowl Projections After 2026-27 Week 11 AP Rankings
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs are back on top of the AP Top 25.
articles.body:
The Georgia Bulldogs are back on top of the AP Top 25.

Kirby Smart's team moved up a spot to No. 1 in the Week 11 rankings after the Miami Hurricanes fell to the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on Saturday.

Notre Dame inched its way closer to the top with a one-spot move up to No. 3, while Miami fell down to No. 5.

The rest of Sunday's poll featured plenty of multi-spot movement, starting with the Tennessee Volunteers, who moved up seven spots to No. 9.

Tennessee was one of 12 teams to move up multiple spots in Sunday's poll. The Vols, Texas Tech Red Raiders and Wake Forest Demon Deacons moved into Nos. 9, 10 and 11, which would be the last three at-large spots in the College Football Playoff.

Georgia is back in a familiar spot on top of the AP Top 25.

The Bulldogs blew out the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday night to make the claim to be the top college football team in the country.

Kirby Smart's team is 8-1 with a clear path to the No. 1 overall seed in the CFB Playoff.

Georgia still has to get through the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks, both of whom are ranked, to finish off SEC play, but if it plays like it did on Saturday, it will be incredibly tough to stop.

At least for now, Georgia can claim that its the favorite to win the playoff, especially with the chaos that's happened across the rankings on a week-by-week basis.

Notre Dame Up to No. 3, Miami Down to No. 5

Notre Dame's win over Miami allowed it to jump to No. 3 in Sunday's poll.

The Fighting Irish played for their playoff life on Saturday because they were ranked No. 11 in the initial CFB Playoff rankings.

Notre Dame was No. 4 in last week's AP poll, but the selection committee thought differently about its resume.

The Irish are two spots ahead of Miami after they beat the ACC side at home.

That's the way it should be after a recent head-to-head result, but now we'll have to wait and see what the selection committee thinks on Tuesday night.

At minimum, Notre Dame should move up multiple spots in the CFB rankings and feel more comfortable about its playoff position.

Miami is safe with one loss, but an extra loss without Malachi Toney might put the Hurricanes in peril, at least in the at-large discussion. The Hurricanes are still the clear favorite to win the ACC's automatic bid.

Tennessee surged up seven spots in Sunday's poll after its win over the Kentucky Wildcats.

The Vols also benefited from a handful of losses from teams in the middle of the rankings.

All of Saturday's results allowed the Vols to move back into a CFB Playoff position with a favorable schedule in front of it.

Tennessee's last ranked matchup is with the LSU Tigers at home in two weeks. It has two road games against unranked conference foes.

In addition to Tennessee, Texas Tech and Wake Forest leaped into what would be the at-large spots in the 12-team playoff field.

Wake Forest is one of the biggest surprises of the season. It is 8-1 and on a collision course to face Miami in the ACC Championship Game.

Texas Tech should be the second Big 12 team in the field behind the Utah Utes. The two best Big 12 sides will likely face off for the conference's automatic bid in the Big 12 Championship Game.

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Bernd Leno, Ronald Araujo, Jair Cunha, Tarik Muharemovic, Nordi Mukiele, Leon Goretzka, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo le Fee, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Thierno Barry, Liam Delap
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Bernd Leno (Fulham): Unbelievable couple of saves from him to keep Fulham in the game. I thought Newcastle should have been three or four up before Fulham got the equaliser.

Ronald Araujo (Liverpool): He is just the difference maker to that Liverpool backline. The injury-time Crystal Palace penalty that denied them a clean sheet was a terrible decision, but when he is in the team, they play better and look more solid.

Jair Cunha (Nottingham Forest): Exceptional. His goal helps, but exceptional at sniffing out the danger. Erling Haaland didn't have a sniff of a goal in Man City's defeat by Forest. Cunha will need to be really good going forward if they're the team Oliver Glasner wants.

Tarik Muharemovic (Leeds United): Many times he got caught one v one against Spurs but showed his ability to be chilled and calm under pressure and make his tackle. Very unassuming.

Nordi Mukiele (Sunderland): He was excellent again. He forced Chelsea to go wide and I think that was the key to them winning the game.

Leon Goretzka (Aston Villa): Although it was 4-4 in the end at Man Utd, Goretzka was a beast. He was calm under pressure and moved the ball really well as well. He obviously got a goal but his passing, movement and the ability to just be calm and handle every situation presented to him was really, really good.

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool): How this guy has not got a new deal I don't know. He keeps coming up big, high energy and he is vitally important to the way Liverpool play. When he is fit and available and firing on all cylinders it feels like they have a chance in this title race.

Enzo Le Fee (Sunderland): Where would Sunderland be without this guy? He has been good, he has been scoring, chipping in with big moments. Also his ability to take the ball when under pressure, take his side up the pitch and also have that little bit of innovative play and free thinking. He is exceptional.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (Everton): Bossed the game for Everton against Coventry. Unbelievable goal but he absolutely bossed it. There was nothing more he could have done. Never gave the ball away, defensively he was solid. Attacking wise - goals and assists.

Thierno Barry (Everton): The two up front pick themselves, but probably the last time I would have them together in the same team. Did really well, two good goals against Coventry and probably should have had a third as well.

Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest): What a game for him and moment he needed. A lot of pressure from the outside, including myself. Hasn't shown up big this season but against his former team Man City, his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca as well, and he turned around and said, 'you know what, I am the man and you should have kept me around'. Scored two unbelievable goals, led the line well and looked physically fitter and stronger. Maybe now that confidence comes through and we see the best of him after the international break.

Mikel Arteta (Arsenal): I am going for Mikel Arteta simply because he has just won the Premier League. Well done. I said at the start of the season that, for me, Arsenal will win the league by 10 points and this weekend they did it. It's November and the season is officially over.

articles.title: Yamal 9.5, Fermin 9.5 | Atletico Madrid 1-2 Barcelona: Player Ratings
articles.summary: League leaders Barcelona locked horns with Atletico Madrid on Sunday night in their final game ahead of the next international break, and the game once again...
articles.body:
League leaders Barcelona locked horns with Atletico Madrid on Sunday night in their final game ahead of the next international break, and the game once again lived up to its billing.

Clashes between the Catalans and the Colchoneros have been high-octane games with unpredictable swings in recent years, and last night's game followed the same theme.

Barcelona started off the game poorly, with Diego Simeone's side deservedly taking the lead and even dominating most of the first half.

Fermin Lopez, however, stepped up with a brace and brought the game back into Barcelona's favour with one goal in each half. The game was in Barcelona's control throughout the second half, and they did well to hold on to their lead.

Barca Universal brings you the player ratings from Atletico Madrid 1-2 Barcelona.

The Barcelona goalkeeper was a busy man against Atletico Madrid, and it is hard to even criticize his performance given how he was let down by his teammates.

Time and time again, the hosts attacked with the same pattern of pushing the ball out wide and looking for a low cross across the face of goal, but Barcelona's defence had no answers to the same.

Instead of being defended, the opportunities thus turned into goalscoring chances, and Garcia did well to keep most at bay.

A horror show from Cancelo. (Picture credit: X/FC Barcelona)

Cancelo was horrific against Atletico Madrid as he looked neither defensively accountable nor convincing in attack.

The Portuguese full-back was poorly positioned for the hosts' opening goal, paving the way for Giuliano Simeone's opener. His passes were miscued, dribbles poorly orchestrated, and his show was an all-round disaster.

The Barcelona centre-back had a tough time holding off Atletico Madrid's attacks and often found himself chasing bodies instead of the ball.

His distribution under pressure was decent, but the pace of the game seemed a bit too fast for Martin's capability, and he was often caught out by the runs from Atletico Madrid's midfield.

Cubarsi's positioning was on-point for most of the game, and he did well to ensure that he held the offside line and led the defence on a night where Atletico Madrid seemed to be the better attacking side.

Yet, he too emerged only second best in most duels he participated in and did not win a single one in the first half. He suffocated under Atletico Madrid's attacking force but was much more free after the break.

Farinas was out of his depth. (Picture credit: X/FC Barcelona)

Farinas was put up to his biggest test yet last night as he took on Alex Baena on the flank, and he struggled to keep up defensively and make the right assessments.

Many of the hosts' attacks began down the right flank, and the youngster was simply unable to read the play and get into the right defensive positions. His combination play was decent, but Hansi Flick was forced to take him off at half-time.

In terms of his distribution, Marc Bernal had a decent half with a good pass completion rate and a decent number of progressive passes.

Beyond that, however, the practical utility of his presence was limited as he did not offer any of the defensive solidity or cover which was expected of him.

Atletico Madrid played through Barcelona's midfield with ease in the first half, and there was seemingly nothing Bernal could do to stop the same. Was far more stable in the second half with Frenkie de Jong also on the field.

Pedri was one of the only two players who had a strong first half against Los Rojiblancos last night, and he simply had no support to make any of his heroics count.

Despite Diego Simeone's men starting off strong and dominating, Pedri was the one player who gave Barcelona some spells of possession, provided a creative spark, and soaked in the pressure from the hosts without crumbling.

He struck the crossbar once and came close to scoring on another occasion in the first half, but he truly opened his wings and began controlling the game only after the break on the night.

Fermin Lopez was lively throughout the game, although he struggled to combine with his teammates in tight spaces for most of the first half.

Just when it seemed like playing through the Atletico Madrid press and compact defense was not Fermin's cup of tea, he found the ball in the middle of the box and struck an equalizer for Barcelona against the run of play.

He then struck again in the 66th minute to score from a tight angle and hand Barcelona the lead on the night, marking an important moment in the game.

Gordon has to offer a lot more. (Picture credit: X/FC Barcelona)

Anthony Gordon does not do a lot wrong in terms of holding on to the ball and passing it around, but for the nth time, his attacking output was nothing extraordinary.

The player struggled to take on his man and create any attacking openings of note against Atletico Madrid. Most of his touches were either horizontal or passes played backwards. He did not add much value as a creative option, a pace runner, or even a good ball-striker.

The captain was barely visible against Atletico Madrid and was constantly marked by the hosts' defense. He struggled to contribute to both the buildup and his responsibility as a target man.

He did get two shots away on the night, but neither hit the target convincingly. Overall, a relatively underwhelming night from the Brazilian star.

Magic at his feet. (Picture credit: X/FC Barcelona)

Lamine Yamal was Barcelona's best player on the night, and simply unstoppable down the right flank even by his astronomical standards.

His dribbles on the night were extraterrestrial and left Alejandro Grimaldo without any chance, and he constantly looked to find his teammates in the box or a direct finish.

In the end, he was the one who made Fermin Lopez's second goal possible, and thus played a key part in the goal that handed Barcelona the lead.

The captain came on in the second half to replace Brian Farinas at right-back and did a solid job in the department. Eventually, he slotted back into midfield, and it is safe to say that his entry added far more control of the game for the Catalans.

articles.summary: Doblete para certificar una remontada que mantiene al Barcelona en lo más alto de la tabla, después de que Giuliano adelante a un Atlético de más a menos y en el que Julián naufraga
articles.body: Fermín por aquí, Fermín por allá. El Atlético había apeado al Barcelona del liderato con el gol de apertura a mayor gloria de Giuliano, pero aquello fue cuestión de tiempo. Porque el equipo local fue de más a menos, sin capacidad alguna para rebelarse y dejando otra vez dudas desde lo físico y desde el banquillo, y porque el equipo visitante fue de menos a más, sin necesidad siquiera de que husmeara esta vez Raphinha, sostenido, eso sí, por Cubarsí y por Pedri. Así que apareció el 7 en la primera parte para resolver una especie de barullo, así que apareció el 7 en la segunda para hacer los honores a una delicia de Lamine. Con la izquierda y con la derecha. No es tan fácil bajar al Barça. De todo había pasado para cuando el Metropolitano rindió homenaje al malogrado Jesús de Miguel con el partido parado. En diez minutos absolutamente frenéticos se registraron un mano a mano, dos largueros y una diana, así que conviene ir por partes y con el freno de mano echado, no vaya a liquidarse esta crónica con el primer tramo de partido. Para empezar, porque el fútbol siempre tiene guiños y porque el verano había sido demasiado largo, Julián topó con una autopista hacia la portería del equipo en el que soñaba con jugar. Tuvo tanto tiempo para pensar desde que arrancó en mediocampo que se le ocurrió incluso la pésima idea de driblar a Joan sin atender a que éste, como sucedió, pudiera palmear la pelota. El Atlético derrochaba adrenalina, pero también toque para superar la zaga azulgrana adelantada. La tuvo después Pubill, cabezazo al travesaño a la salida de un córner, pero Pedri respondió enseguida con su primera incursión para topar también con la madera. No se vayan, aún hay más: una excelente apertura de Kang-in sirvió para que Julián se hiciera el quite del perdón asistiendo a Giuliano para el primero, que convirtió el Metropolitano en una jaula de grillos desde el liderato momentáneo. Diez minutos, conviene insistir. Simeone y Flick habían apostado por el producto nacional para sus respectivos mediocampos, Koke y Barrios en el doble pivote local, Bernal haciendo de Rodri. El Barça fue ganando metros poco a poco, a partir de lo que era sospecha y tornó en evidencia, Grimaldo iba a pasarlo mal ante Lamine, pero el Atlético siempre mantuvo la idea de hacer daño a la contra, de hecho Kang-in y sobre todo Julián volvieron a probar suerte para encontrarse con Joan. Pubill y Cubarsí sostenían a las zagas respectivas, pero el despliegue anteriorresultaba imposible de sostener para la tropa local, demasiado contemplativa en tres cuartos, de manera que aquello iba virando en lo que a la dirección respecta. No parecía dar para el empate antes del descanso... pero dio. Porque la última correría de Pedri llegó hasta el balcón del área y, sobre todo, hasta la zurda de Fermín. Que no avisa. Que ejecuta. Podía entenderse que el Barcelona tocaría a rebato y que golpe iba a tener un efecto demoledor para el Atlético, sobre todo con un doble pivote en el que el 6 sale de lesión y el 8 parece jugar con miedo a entrar en ella. Efectivamente, Lamine probó suerte dos veces en cuanto aquello se reanudó. Flick había envidado con De Jong por Fariñas, sin sorprender tanto el cambio como la constatación de que el neerlandés se iba a situar justo en el espacio que dejaba su compañero: en el lateral derecho. El rival no se sintió concernido, en todo caso: casi nunca apretó por ahí. Por el medio sí encontró una salida, otra vez para citar a Julián, otra vez para que la desaprovechara. Carente de velocidad, se la jugó desde lejos con una vaselina inocua. Llegados a ese punto el Metropolitano se había cansado del argentino, así que la aparición de Sorloth como primer cambio trajo música de viento por el sustituido, que fue Kang-in, que no por el sustituto. El equipo del Cholo boqueaba ya, pero al míster se le hizo de noche con el resto del carrusel. Ni siquiera entendió conveniente agotarlo atendiendo a que Lamine ya había encontrado a Fermín para cuando hizo los siguientes movimientos. Flick por su parte terminó prescindiendo de Fermín y moviendo por fin a De Jong, aunque tanto daba ya. El tramo final resultó absolutamente prescindible en clave de un Atlético al que la semana parece haber puesto en su sitio. El del Barça sigue siendo el que era: el primer puesto.
